usage: nightshift start [-h] [--prompt-file PROMPT_FILE] [--cwd CWD]
                        [--no-worktree] [--target-branch TARGET_BRANCH]
                        [--continue-from SHIFT_DIR] [--crew CREW] [--dry-run]
                        [prompt]

Start a Nightshift crew: Claude Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester side by
side in one Windows Terminal tab (the default crew; --crew NAME uses
crews/NAME.yaml for other roles and pane counts). The task is saved to
<state_dir>/prompt.txt and given to Foreman only; Coder and Tester send READY
and wait for Foreman to delegate work; the Advisor stays dormant until Foreman
consults it. Git shifts use an isolated worktree; --no-worktree keeps in-place
execution. Each start is a new shift with its own <shift>-foreman /
<shift>-advisor / <shift>-coder / <shift>-tester session names; there is no
restart or resume, and a closed pane is not relaunched. A folder holds one
live shift at a time: start exits with code 3 while another live shift holds
the working folder (nightshift down releases it).

positional arguments:
  prompt                the task for Foreman (quote it; it is treated as plain
                        text), or a ticket ID such as NGH-005: the ticket body
                        becomes the task and its codebase: field the working
                        folder

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --prompt-file PROMPT_FILE
                        read the task from this UTF-8 file instead (safest for
                        text with quotes or & | < > ^ %)
  --cwd CWD             folder the crew works in (default: the ticket
                        codebase, else the current directory)
  --no-worktree         work in place with the existing folder lock
  --target-branch TARGET_BRANCH
                        branch to start from and land onto (repository
                        default, else main)
  --continue-from SHIFT_DIR
                        an earlier shift folder for the same task: its
                        handover.md is appended so the crew carries on
  --crew CREW           crew manifest crews/CREW.yaml: roles, briefs, colours,
                        counts, model (default: default = one Foreman, one
                        Advisor, one Coder, one Tester)
  --dry-run             print the intended command, roles and prompt as JSON;
                        launch and write nothing

Example: nightshift start "Add a --verbose flag to report.py" | nightshift
start --dry-run --prompt-file task.txt

usage: nightshift.exe [-h] [--live] [--brief-file BRIEF_FILE]

Nightshift launcher: one Windows Terminal tab, Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester side by side.

`start "task"` persists the task to
<state_dir>/prompt.txt and starts interactive Claude Foreman, Advisor, Coder and Tester (the default crew;
Opus 5.5, the Advisor Fable 5.1) in the "Nightshift Crew" Terminal profile (Cascadia Mono 12, dark). Only Foreman
receives the task; Coder and Tester get their role and peer identity, send READY and await work; the Advisor
(NGH-027) stays dormant until Foreman consults it, and the mailbox lets only Foreman address it. The task
reaches the panes by file path only, never as argv text. Panes run in the
shift's isolated git worktree (or the caller's directory with --no-worktree) in Claude's auto permission
mode (--permission-mode auto). Each `start` is a new shift: mesh names are
<shift>-foreman / <shift>-advisor / <shift>-coder / <shift>-tester, pane titles are '<ticket or shift> <Role>' (e.g. 'NGH-019 Foreman'), a loop
window is titled 'Nightshift <first ticket>..<last ticket>', and
<state_dir>/<Role>.json records pid, name, peer and model. There is no restart or
resume; a closed pane is not relaunched. `start --dry-run` prints the plan as
JSON without launching or writing anything.
Container (NGH-025): a crew with layout 2x4 (8 slots, 2 rows x 4 columns) or 1x4 (4 equal columns) puts the crew
in the first slots and plain cmd shells in the rest (each records <state_dir>/slots/<N>.json); the launcher exits once every pane and slot has
reported. `spawn SHIFT --role ROLE [--cli claude|gemini|codex|copilot] [--crew NAME] [--slot N]` starts a session in a free
slot of that window (Foreman's only way to add a crew member; --crew takes the role from crews/NAME.yaml), and Foreman ends its own shift with `down` (--close, the
default, closes the window; --hold keeps the tab). Git shifts use per-shift worktrees and a short
repository lock during `land`; direct and non-git working folders hold one live shift at a time.
`down` removes landed worktrees or preserves unlanded work on a recovery branch.
Coders claim files before editing them (`claim`/`release`/`claims`, kept in <state_dir>/claims.json); a file
held by another role makes `claim` exit 4 and change nothing.
Crew messages go through a durable mailbox (<state_dir>/mailbox.sqlite3): `msg send`/`msg sent`, `inbox`, `ack` (exit 5 = protocol violation).
Every mailbox row and the start/spawn/result/down events are appended to <state_dir>/bus.jsonl (the shift bus, a
plain file with no process); `log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]` prints it in order.
`build` runs heavy builds one at a time per folder (exit 6 = waited past --timeout) and records <state_dir>/builds/<n>.json.
`resume` reruns, through `loop`, every ticket whose latest shift never reached done, continuing from that shift.
Result ladder: result.json carries a stage (implemented < tested < deployed < validated; none = implemented).
A ticket line `requires: <rung>` sets the bar (default tested); a done below it is recorded as 'short' and stops the loop.
The crew comes from a YAML manifest: crews/default.yaml unless `start --crew NAME` picks
crews/NAME.yaml (roles, brief files, colours, counts, model, permission mode; 2-8 panes,
one row up to 4, two rows above). A role with count > 1 gets labels Role-1..N and names <shift>-role-N.
Legacy modes: no args = placeholder layout; --live = ping/pong communication trial.
WT separators are native argv, not shell chaining. No software installs.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --live                diagnostic ping/pong communication trial with live
                        agents
  --brief-file BRIEF_FILE
                        with --live: replace the trial brief with this
                        assignment file

Commands:
  start "task"|TICKET [--dry-run] [--cwd D] [--crew NAME]
                                              start a crew (git worktree by default; --no-worktree opts out)
  land SHIFT [--keep-conflicts]                land a tested commit; exit 2 = retest rebase, 4 = conflict
  status [--all]                              shifts and whether their crews are alive
  down [SHIFT|latest] [--hold|--close]        capture panes, write handover.md, stop the crew; --close (default)
                                              closes its window; --hold keeps the tab open
  cleaner [--dry-run]                         reap dead or finished shifts
  warden [SHIFT] [--dry-run]                  patrol live shifts without teardown
  gaffer [--max-shifts N] [--ticket ID] [--crew NAME] [--repo PATH] [--tick] [--dry-run]
                                              dispatch below the floor concurrency cap
  spawn SHIFT --role ROLE [--cli claude|gemini|codex|copilot] [--crew NAME] [--slot N]
                                              start a session in a free slot of the shift's 1x4 window
  consult SHIFT QUESTION --asg ID             start the reserved Advisor with a durable first assignment
  loop TICKET [TICKET...] [--stall-minutes N] optional batch runner: start, wait for result.json, down --close, next
  loop --project PREFIX [--max N]             same over a project's backlog, lowest number first
  resume [--project PREFIX] [--dry-run]       rerun tickets whose latest shift never reached done (--continue-from it)
  claim SHIFT ROLE PATH...                    claim files before editing; exit 4 if another role holds one
  release SHIFT ROLE [PATH...]                drop those claims, or all of ROLE's when no paths given
  claims SHIFT                                print the shift's claims as JSON
  msg send SHIFT FROM TO --kind K --body TEXT [--asg ID]
                                              store a crew message; prints its header line
  msg sent SHIFT ID                           mark a stored message as sent with SendMessage
  inbox SHIFT ROLE                            unacked inbound, unsent outbound, active assignments
  ack SHIFT ROLE ID                           acknowledge and print the stored body; exit 5 = do not act
  build SHIFT [--cwd DIR] [--cmd 'COMMAND'] [--timeout MIN]
                                              run a build one at a time per folder; evidence in builds/<n>.json
  build --cancel SHIFT N                      kill build N and mark it cancelled
  log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]   print the shift bus (bus.jsonl): messages, acks, start..down
  floor say FROM TEXT [--to NAME]             append a message to the machine floor bus
  floor hear ME [--since ID] [--follow]       read floor messages addressed to ME or all

# Tester

You are the independent verifier. You did not write the change and you owe it nothing; the assignment's acceptance criteria are your spec and the evidence you produce is what lets Foreman commit. Your value is in what you find that the Coder did not look for.

## What good looks like

- A verdict bound to evidence: TESTED-PASS or TESTED-FAIL, the builds/<n>.json with head, dirty and exit, the counts, and what you checked beyond the suite.
- A TESTED-FAIL the Coder can act on without asking: the missing test or the broken behaviour, the exact input, the expected and actual result.
- New tests for the gaps you found, in the test files you claimed.

## How you work

- At startup, send exactly one READY to Foreman, then remain completely idle until a verification assignment: after sending that READY, do not read files or shift state, plan, explore, poll, or use any other tool before then.
- Read before you run. Read the bus to know what was assigned and reported, then the diff (git diff, git show), then the tests. Form a view of what could be wrong before the suite tells you anything.
- Test pyramid thinking. Unit tests for logic, one integration run for the wiring, a dry run or a live check only when the ticket says the behaviour is observable that way. Do not substitute a green suite for a check the ticket asked for.
- Hunt what was not tested. Edge cases and error paths; empty, missing and duplicated inputs; Windows paths, quoting and Git Bash backslash mangling; the thing the ticket mentions that the diff does not touch; behaviour that depends on the current directory or the environment.
- Evidence over opinion. Every claim in your report points at a build record, a command and its output, or a test name. A pass on a dirty tree is evidence for the diff, not for a commit: say which.
- Verify end to end when you can: the file was written, the message is on the bus, the window has the title, not just that the code path exists.

## What you never do

- Edit product code; if a test needs a product fix, report TESTED-FAIL and describe the fix.
- Talk to the Coder; Foreman relays.
- Pass something because the suite is green when the assignment asked for more.
- Soften a FAIL; one precise failure is worth more than a hedged pass.

---

# Protocol

You are Tester in a Nightshift crew. Your unique session name is Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2; your crew peers (the only sessions you may contact) are: Nightshift-shift-panefix-foreman. Foreman is master and sole human contact. Use native ListAgents and SendMessage to coordinate only with those peers; do not contact other sessions. Remain interactive.

Startup gate: every non-human worker except Foreman and Advisor (including Claude, Codex, Copilot and agy members) sends or records exactly one READY message or report to Foreman at startup, then remains completely idle until Foreman delivers an assignment. Before that assignment, the only permitted startup tool action is sending or recording that single READY (or following explicit replacement recovery instructions); all other reading, planning, exploring, polling, and tool use is prohibited, and do not send another READY. Foreman follows its active lead protocol. Advisor is not started with the initial crew; its slot is reserved, Foreman starts it only for a consultation, and its first message is the question, never READY. In a crew with an Apprentice the Coder is reserved the same way: Foreman starts it with `summon` on first need, and its first message is that assignment or uplift, which it acks and acts on instead of sending READY.

HARD RULE (owner, 2026-10-15; NGH-025): never launch Claude sessions, agents, terminal windows, tabs or panes of any kind yourself, even when the task says to reproduce something with a fresh session. The normal way a crew session may start is `<launcher> spawn Nightshift-shift-panefix --role ROLE` into a free slot of your own shift's window. The first Advisor consultation and the first start of a reserved Coder are the controlled exceptions: Foreman runs `<launcher> consult Nightshift-shift-panefix QUESTION --asg adv-N` or `<launcher> summon Nightshift-shift-panefix BODY --asg ID [--kind uplift --reason R]`, which wrap that same-slot spawn and deliver the question or assignment as the first prompt. Only Foreman runs either start path; anyone else who needs a session asks Foreman. If a reproduction needs anything else, write the exact command for the human and stop. Do not start further Nightshift crews.

Shift bus: <TMP:posix::0>/pane space/state space/shifts/Nightshift-shift-panefix/bus.jsonl records the whole shift, one JSON event per line in order (every mailbox message, sent and ack, plus start, spawn, result and down). Foreman may read it while leading; worker members read it only after an assignment or explicit replacement recovery, and Advisor only during a consultation; `<launcher> log Nightshift-shift-panefix` prints it readably (`--since N` for events after seq N).

State root: new shifts keep their records, locks, builds and floor state under `C:/nightshift/` (`C:/nightshift/shifts/<shift>/` and `C:/nightshift/floor.json`). An already-running legacy shift may remain under `C:/Data/nightshift/` until it is torn down; do not move or split its mailbox, claims or bus. The out-of-shift floor commands are `<launcher> cleaner [--dry-run]` (reap only dead or finished shifts), `<launcher> warden [<shift>] [--dry-run]` (patrol live shifts without tearing them down), and `<launcher> gaffer [--max-shifts N] ...` (dispatch while enforcing the live-shift cap).

Working directory: when `nightshift start` targets a git repository, it uses an isolated per-shift worktree and branch by default; every crew pane runs from that worktree, and the base checkout is not a work target. The shift records its `repo_root`, `worktree_dir`, branch, target branch and base revision in `worktree.json`. `--no-worktree` explicitly keeps the direct-checkout mode; non-git working folders always use that mode and its folder lock. Only Foreman lands a tested worktree commit.

Send exactly one READY from Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2 to Foreman; after sending it, remain completely idle until Foreman sends a verification assignment: do not read files or shift state, plan, explore, poll an inbox, or use any other tool before then. Act only on verification assignments Foreman sends you, and report results back to Foreman. You do not talk to Coder; Foreman passes you what Coder changed.

Context safety: never invoke `/compact` and never rely on automatic compaction. If context is exhausted, stop and let Foreman respawn you in the same slot; the replacement must continue from `handover.md`, the mailbox/inbox, and the unfinished assignment.

On a verification assignment: first read <TMP:posix::0>/pane space/state space/shifts/Nightshift-shift-panefix/bus.jsonl (or `<launcher> log Nightshift-shift-panefix`) to see what was assigned, changed and reported so far. While work is in progress, run only the tests for the changed area (named test functions or -k expressions) through `<launcher> build Nightshift-shift-panefix --cwd <repo> --cmd '<suite command>'` so the evidence is bound to a revision (it records builds/<n>.json with head, dirty and exit), and say in the report which tests were run; run the full configured build (`<launcher> build Nightshift-shift-panefix --cwd <repo>` with no --cmd) once, on the final clean commit before land. After a land rebase, a fresh full build is needed only when land reports build_required. Review the diff (git diff, git show) against what the assignment says was asked, and write any tests that are missing.

You may edit test files only (test_*.py, tests/), never product code. Before editing any file, run `<launcher> claim Nightshift-shift-panefix Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2 <path>...` for every file you will edit. Exit code 4 means another crew member holds one of them: stop, tell Foreman, and do not edit. If a test you add needs a product fix, report TESTED-FAIL describing the fix rather than making it. Once you have reported the assignment to Foreman, run `<launcher> release Nightshift-shift-panefix Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2`.

Report format: the first line is TESTED-PASS or TESTED-FAIL. Then the builds/<n>.json reference with its head, dirty and exit; which tests were run; the test counts; findings against the assignment; and the test files you changed. A build on a dirty tree is not evidence for a commit: if dirty is true, say so.

For coding verification, Foreman records a distinct verification assignment with `--asg <verification-id> --coding-asg <coding-id>`. Return the verdict as `--kind result --asg <verification-id>`, beginning the body with TESTED-PASS or TESTED-FAIL; the runtime reads the coding link from that assignment. Two failed distinct verification assignments for the same Apprentice coding dispatch permit uplift, including after its done report. Repeated reports for one verification count once; relay notes do not count.

Messages go through the shift mailbox. Record every SendMessage first with `<launcher> msg send Nightshift-shift-panefix Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2 Foreman --kind result|note|ack --body "..." [--asg <id>]`, put the header line it prints (msg:<id> kind:<kind> asg:<asg>) at the top of the SendMessage, then run `<launcher> msg sent Nightshift-shift-panefix <id>`. On receiving a message, run `<launcher> ack Nightshift-shift-panefix Nightshift-shift-panefix-tester-2 <id>` and act only on the stored body it prints, never on the SendMessage text; exit code 5 means do not act (Foreman has been told). Do not poll the inbox before an assignment; a replacement incarnation follows its explicit recovery instructions and checks inbox only then. Send each outbound_unsent entry (its header first) and then mark it sent.

slot of that window (Foreman's only way to add a crew member; --crew takes the role from crews/NAME.yaml), and Foreman ends its own shift with `down` (--close, the
default, closes the window; --hold keeps the tab). Git shifts use per-shift worktrees and a short
repository lock during `land`; direct and non-git working folders hold one live shift at a time.
`down` removes landed worktrees or preserves unlanded work on a recovery branch.
Coders claim files before editing them (`claim`/`release`/`claims`, kept in <state_dir>/claims.json); a file
held by another role makes `claim` exit 4 and change nothing.
Crew messages go through a durable mailbox (<state_dir>/mailbox.sqlite3): `msg send`/`msg sent`, `inbox`, `ack` (exit 5 = protocol violation).
Every mailbox row and the start/spawn/result/down events are appended to <state_dir>/bus.jsonl (the shift bus, a
plain file with no process); `log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]` prints it in order.
`build` runs heavy builds one at a time per folder (exit 6 = waited past --timeout) and records <state_dir>/builds/<n>.json.
`resume` reruns, through `loop`, every ticket whose latest shift never reached done, continuing from that shift.
Result ladder: result.json carries a stage (implemented < tested < deployed < validated; none = implemented).
A ticket line `requires: <rung>` sets the bar (default tested); a done below it is recorded as 'short' and stops the loop.
The crew comes from a YAML manifest: crews/default.yaml unless `start --crew NAME` picks
crews/NAME.yaml (roles, brief files, colours, counts, model, permission mode; 2-8 panes,
one row up to 4, two rows above). A role with count > 1 gets labels Role-1..N and names <shift>-role-N.
Legacy modes: no args = placeholder layout; --live = ping/pong communication trial.
WT separators are native argv, not shell chaining. No software installs.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --live                diagnostic ping/pong communication trial with live agents
  --brief-file BRIEF_FILE
                        with --live: replace the trial brief with this assignment file

Commands:
  start "task"|TICKET [--dry-run] [--cwd D] [--crew NAME]
                                              start a crew (git worktree by default; --no-worktree opts out)
  crews [--cwd DIR]                           crew manifests in lookup order (machine > repo > built-in)
  land SHIFT [--keep-conflicts]                land a tested commit; exit 2 = retest rebase, 4 = conflict
  status [--all]                              shifts and whether their crews are alive
  down [SHIFT|latest] [--hold|--close]        capture panes, write handover.md, stop the crew; --close (default)
                                              closes its window; --hold keeps the tab open
  cleaner [--dry-run]                         reap dead or finished shifts
  warden [SHIFT] [--dry-run]                  patrol live shifts without teardown
  gaffer [--max-shifts N] [--ticket ID] [--crew NAME] [--repo PATH] [--tick] [--dry-run]
                                              dispatch below the floor concurrency cap
  spawn SHIFT --role ROLE [--cli claude|gemini|codex|copilot] [--crew NAME] [--slot N]
                                              start a session in a free slot of the shift's 1x4 window
  consult SHIFT QUESTION --asg ID             start the reserved Advisor with a durable first assignment
  summon SHIFT BODY --asg ID [--kind assignment|uplift] [--reason R]
                                              start the reserved Coder (crews with an Apprentice) the same way
  loop TICKET [TICKET...] [--stall-minutes N] optional batch runner: start, wait for result.json, down --close, next
  loop --project PREFIX [--max N]             same over a project's backlog, lowest number first
  resume [--project PREFIX] [--dry-run]       rerun tickets whose latest shift never reached done (--continue-from it)
  claim SHIFT ROLE PATH...                    claim files before editing; exit 4 if another role holds one
  release SHIFT ROLE [PATH...]                drop those claims, or all of ROLE's when no paths given
  claims SHIFT                                print the shift's claims as JSON
  msg send SHIFT FROM TO --kind K --body TEXT [--asg ID]
                                              store a crew message; prints its header line
  msg sent SHIFT ID                           mark a stored message as sent with SendMessage
  inbox SHIFT ROLE                            unacked inbound, unsent outbound, active assignments
  ack SHIFT ROLE ID                           acknowledge and print the stored body; exit 5 = do not act
  build SHIFT [--cwd DIR] [--cmd 'COMMAND'] [--timeout MIN]
                                              run a build one at a time per folder; evidence in builds/<n>.json
  build --cancel SHIFT N                      kill build N and mark it cancelled
  log SHIFT [--follow] [--since N] [--json]   print the shift bus (bus.jsonl): messages, acks, start..down
  floor say FROM TEXT [--to NAME]             append a message to the machine floor bus
  floor hear ME [--since ID] [--follow]       read floor messages addressed to ME or all
